schema.era_role: What the leader actually IS during each era block. Roles shift; a guide written for one role misleads in the next.
schema.caveats: Specific traps. Things the strategy summary implies are free but are not.
schema.guide_must_account_for: What a turn-by-turn guide needs as structure, not content. Checkpoints, gates, monitors, abort conditions.
schema.guide_shape: The structural type of guide this leader needs. One of: Countdown, Gate, Monitor, Front-Load, Dead-Phase, Linear.

leaders.name: Gilgamesh

era_role.ancient_classical: Primary aggressor. The War-Cart window is the entire identity.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Digester. Turning captured cities into functional infrastructure.
era_role.industrial_modern: Generic wide empire. Leader ability contributes nothing.
era_role.atomic_information: Wins or loses on empire size banked 150 turns earlier.

caveats: War-Carts obsolete and their upgrade path is expensive; the unit advantage is a window, not a standing army.
Captured cities arrive with no infrastructure and immediately tax amenities and loyalty.
The barbarian outpost reward encourages leaving camps alive, which is also how you get raided.
guide_must_account_for: A hard stop-conquering turn, after which the guide switches entirely to consolidation.
An amenity and loyalty checkpoint after every single capture, not at fixed intervals.
An abort condition: if the first neighbor is not taken by the deadline, what replaces the plan.

leaders.name: Amanitore

era_role.ancient_classical: Simultaneous aggressor and district engine. Rare double role.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Infrastructure snowball off permanently cheaper districts.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong generic empire; the military identity is long gone.

caveats: Nubian Pyramid placement is permanent. A bad early siting is a permanent tax.
Pitati Archers fall off hard once Crossbowmen exist; the window is narrower than it feels.
The district production discount does nothing for purchased districts.
guide_must_account_for: Pyramid siting resolved before the first district is queued anywhere.
An explicit archer-window countdown tied to opponent tech, not turn number.
The pivot turn from military production to district spam.

leaders.name: Montezuma

era_role.ancient_classical: Raider harvesting Builders rather than territory.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Wide empire with a luxury-scaled army.
era_role.industrial_modern: Luxury combat bonus diluted by inflated base strength values.

caveats: Captured Builders are worthless without a queued improvement plan to spend charges on.
The combat bonus counts distinct luxuries, not copies. Ten of one resource is one bonus.
Warring everyone removes the trade partners you need to acquire luxuries you lack.
guide_must_account_for: A Builder-charge sink list maintained in parallel with the war plan.
Luxury acquisition tracked as its own objective line, separate from conquest.
A diplomacy floor: which civs must stay peaceful to keep the luxury count climbing.

leaders.name: Tomyris

era_role.ancient_classical: Swarm. Peak power.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still cavalry, no longer dominant.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ability contributes nothing.

caveats: Heal-on-kill requires kills. Grinding against walls with no field units to kill is where the engine dies.
Duplicate unit training doubles maintenance, and the gold cost arrives before the payoff.
Nothing about the kit produces a standing yield. If the swarm does not take cities, there is no residue.
guide_must_account_for: A named target list with per-target deadlines, because the whole plan is time-boxed.
A gold and maintenance checkpoint before each new wave of units.
An explicit failure branch: what this civ becomes if the early war stalls.

leaders.name: Simon Bolivar

era_role.ancient_classical: Accelerated settling. Settlers and Builders move faster than anyone's.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Fast wars with stacked Comandante Generals.
era_role.industrial_modern: Still faster than everyone. The bonus never stops applying.
era_role.atomic_information: Still relevant. One of the few kits with no expiry.

caveats: Comandante Generals are era-bound and retire; banking them without using them wastes the ability.
Movement advantage shrinks on rough terrain and once rivals have roads and railroads.
The bonus is broad but shallow. It amplifies a plan, it does not supply one.
guide_must_account_for: General expiry tracked per era, with a use-or-lose prompt at each era transition.
Settle radius planning that assumes the extra movement point, otherwise the advantage evaporates unused.
A primary victory path chosen separately, since the ability is path-agnostic.

leaders.name: Alexander

era_role.ancient_classical: Encampment build-out and first wars.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Continuous war with no domestic penalty.
era_role.industrial_modern: Still warring, but tech parity becomes the binding constraint.

caveats: Peace switches the kit off. There is no reward for consolidation phases.
No war weariness is not no unhappiness. Loyalty and amenities in captured cities still bite.
Science from unit training only pays while you keep training. Stopping stops the science.
guide_must_account_for: A rolling target queue with the next war identified before the current one ends.
Loyalty, not weariness, as the monitored stat during occupation.
A continuous unit production line treated as a science building, not a military decision.

leaders.name: Gorgo

era_role.ancient_classical: Barbarian farming into an early civic lead.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Culture lead cashed into governments and policy cards ahead of schedule.
era_role.industrial_modern: Combat culture diluted; the lead must already exist.

caveats: Culture comes from killing units, not from capturing cities. A clean city grab pays nothing.
Barbarian supply dries up as the map is settled, and that is usually before the ability stops mattering.
The culture is only worth what you unlock with it; hoarding it is the common failure.
guide_must_account_for: A kill-source pipeline as a maintained resource, with a plan for when barbarians run out.
A pre-committed civic target list so the culture spike converts immediately.
A warning that siege-heavy, low-kill warfare produces almost nothing for her.

leaders.name: Ambiorix

era_role.ancient_classical: Clustered rush at maximum effectiveness.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Falls off as fronts widen and clustering becomes a liability.
era_role.industrial_modern: Nothing.

caveats: Clustered units are exactly what siege and later area damage are designed to punish.
Culture from training units encourages building an army the economy cannot maintain.
The adjacency bonus rewards formations, which is a skill the guide has to teach, not a build order.
guide_must_account_for: Formation guidance as an actual step, not a build queue.
A maintenance checkpoint, since the culture incentive pushes toward overbuilding.
The turn at which clustering stops being an advantage and becomes a target.

leaders.name: Shaka

era_role.ancient_classical: Genuinely weak. Survival phase with no leader-specific advantage.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Corps snowball with auto-upgrade on capture.
era_role.industrial_modern: Advantage shrinks once every civ has Corps and Armies access.

caveats: The early game is a real vulnerability, not a slow start. Getting rushed ends the game before the kit exists.
The +5 edge is an edge over civs without Corps. It shrinks to nothing once everyone has them.
The go signal is a civic unlock, not a turn number, and it varies by game.
guide_must_account_for: A defensive phase with its own complete build order, treated as a real phase and not filler.
A gate condition (Mercenaries) that triggers the transition, replacing any fixed turn.
A closing window warning: the snowball must be underway before rivals reach Corps parity.

leaders.name: Cyrus

era_role.ancient_classical: Surprise war bursts against unprepared neighbors.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Same pattern, higher grievance cost.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ten turns no longer crosses the distances involved.
era_role.atomic_information: Diplomatically radioactive with little to show.

caveats: Grievances accumulate permanently and invite coalitions. The cost is paid long after the war.
The ten turns start at declaration, so any staging done after the DoW is time spent from the budget.
Repeated surprise wars foreclose every diplomatic and city-state avenue for the rest of the game.
guide_must_account_for: A staging checklist that must fully complete before the declaration turn.
A grievance budget tracked as a resource with a ceiling.
A turn-10 checkpoint with an explicit abort-and-peace branch if the objective is not taken.

leaders.name: Genghis Khan

era_role.ancient_classical: Horsemen pressure and trade route positioning.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Knights and Keshigs with captured cavalry compounding.
era_role.industrial_modern: Cavalry still functional, no longer decisive.

caveats: The trade route must reach and survive at the target, which means setting it up well before hostility.
Capturing defeated cavalry only pays against civs that actually field cavalry.
Horse resource access is a hard prerequisite the ability does not provide.
guide_must_account_for: Trade route dispatch as an explicit pre-war step with its own lead time.
A horse and strategic resource audit before committing to the plan.
Target selection filtered by whether the enemy fields capturable units.

leaders.name: Chandragupta

era_role.ancient_classical: Largely dormant. The casus belli is not available immediately.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak, in narrow bursts against adjacent targets.
era_role.industrial_modern: The movement burst no longer covers the map.

caveats: The bonus requires a specific casus belli, so the real start turn is a civic unlock, not turn one.
The target must be adjacent. A distant neighbor makes the whole kit inapplicable.
Ten turns is the entire window, and it is spent moving as much as fighting.
guide_must_account_for: The civic unlock as the actual opening of the plan, with a defined pre-gate build order.
Pre-positioning completed before the war declaration.
A target viability check based on distance, run before committing to the strategy.

leaders.name: Harald Hardrada

era_role.ancient_classical: Longship raiding as primary income.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still raiding, with diminishing returns per coast.
era_role.industrial_modern: The pillage economy is obsolete; coastal defenses outclass raiders.

caveats: Pillage yields deplete per tile. The same coastline does not pay twice.
Raiding produces income but never territory, so the empire does not grow while the ability works.
Landlocked or low-coast maps flatly disable the strategy.
guide_must_account_for: A parallel domestic build plan, since raiding alone never compounds.
A trigger for when to stop raiding and start actually taking cities.
A map viability check before the strategy is recommended at all.

leaders.name: Matthias Corvinus

era_role.ancient_classical: Envoy and gold economy. Not yet a military civ.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Levied proxy armies at full effect.
era_role.industrial_modern: Levied city-state units lag badly behind modern militaries.

caveats: Levy costs scale, so the strategy gets more expensive exactly as you use it more.
Suzerainty can be taken mid-campaign, which removes the army you are currently fighting with.
Levied units revert. Nothing you levy is ever yours.
guide_must_account_for: A gold reserve threshold checked before each levy, not after.
Suzerainty defense as an ongoing per-turn concern, tracked like a resource.
Captured city consolidation, since the cities are the only permanent gain.

leaders.name: Suleiman

era_role.ancient_classical: Ordinary civ. No leader advantage. Survive and develop.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Begins to matter as siege becomes relevant.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Siege specialization against fortified capitals.

caveats: There is no early identity at all. The guide has to fill roughly 100 turns with generic play.
Janissary recruitment costs population, which competes directly with growth.
The unique governor needs establishment time in place before it affects anything.
guide_must_account_for: A complete generic early build order, because the leader supplies no direction there.
Governor placement scheduled well ahead of the intended war, not at declaration.
A defensive floor for the long dormant phase, since the kit offers no early protection.

leaders.name: Lautaro

era_role.ancient_classical: Dormant. No Golden Ages exist to punish yet.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Opportunistic spoiler against whoever is ahead.
era_role.industrial_modern: Same role, dependent on rival era scores.

caveats: The trigger belongs to other players. There are eras where the ability simply does not apply.
Loyalty flipping requires population pressure to already be in place; the kills alone do not do it.
Verify the direction of the ability before writing the guide: the loyalty pressure keys off kills in his own territory.
guide_must_account_for: Rival era score as a monitored per-turn stat, since it determines whether the kit is live.
A default plan for eras where no rival is in a Golden Age.
Loyalty pressure groundwork built before the opportunity appears, not in response to it.

leaders.name: Trajan

era_role.ancient_classical: Aggressive settling with free culture in every city.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Compounding civic lead from accumulated Monuments.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ordinary large empire; ability contribution is baked in already.
era_role.atomic_information: No ongoing effect, but the head start persists.

caveats: Free Monuments make expansion feel free. Amenities, gold, and loyalty are still real limits.
Automatic roads move invaders through your territory as efficiently as they move Legions.
The bonus is front-loaded per city, so late-founded cities contribute much less.
guide_must_account_for: A settle-rate cap tied to amenity and gold capacity rather than available land.
A culture spend plan, since the advantage is worthless unbanked.
Diminishing returns on cities founded after the culture lead is already established.

leaders.name: Hojo Tokimune

era_role.ancient_classical: Tight city placement and the first district clusters.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Compact high-yield complexes across every city.
era_role.industrial_modern: Still strong, though spacing begins to cap growth.

caveats: Tight spacing that helps adjacency also caps late-game population per city.
The half-cost applies to three district types only; everything else is normal price.
Adjacency requires deliberate placement order, so build sequence is a real decision.
guide_must_account_for: A city spacing plan drawn before the second Settler moves.
District placement order as an explicit sequence, since later placements depend on earlier ones.
The tradeoff point where tighter spacing starts costing more than the adjacency returns.

leaders.name: Qin Shi Huang

era_role.ancient_classical: Builder spam converting charges directly into Wonders.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Ability expired. Living off the wonders already banked.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ordinary civ with an unusually good wonder collection.

caveats: Charges spent on Wonders are charges not spent on tile improvements, so the terrain stays weak.
A rival completing the wonder first wastes the charges entirely with no refund.
The ability covers Ancient and Classical wonders only. It has a hard expiry.
guide_must_account_for: A wonder shortlist with pre-planned fallbacks for each one being sniped.
A Builder charge budget explicitly split between wonders and improvements.
The era boundary where the ability stops, treated as a scheduled transition.

leaders.name: Frederick Barbarossa

era_role.ancient_classical: City-state bullying and expansion. Ability not yet leveraged.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Hansa clusters begin compounding.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak industrial output.
era_role.atomic_information: Strong production base carries into any victory type.

caveats: The extra district still requires the population to staff and the production to build it.
Hansa adjacency depends on Commercial Hubs and resources being placed correctly first.
Bullying city-states creates lasting grievances and forfeits suzerainty options.
guide_must_account_for: District cap tracked per city, since the extra slot is the whole ability.
Hansa and Commercial Hub placement planned jointly, before either is built.
A decision point on bullying versus envoy investment, because they are mutually exclusive.

leaders.name: Pachacuti

era_role.ancient_classical: Mountain settling. Slow but structurally sound.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: High-population fortified cities coming online.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong tall empire with natural defense.

caveats: A start without mountains makes the leader ordinary at best. Start roll variance is the highest on the roster.
Mountains block your own unit movement as effectively as they block invaders.
Early production from mountain-heavy terrain is low even with the ability.
guide_must_account_for: A start assessment step with a genuine go or no-go on the position.
Terrace Farm placement planned against mountain adjacency from the first Builder.
An early production supplement plan, since the terrain does not provide one.

leaders.name: John Curtin

era_role.ancient_classical: Passive. Appeal-aware settling with no active ability use.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Baiting aggression to trigger production bursts.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Bursts dumped into high-cost projects.

caveats: The trigger requires being attacked, which you do not control and cannot schedule.
Baiting aggression risks actually losing cities to a competent aggressor.
A burst with nothing queued is a burst wasted; the ten turns do not wait.
guide_must_account_for: A pre-queued list of expensive builds kept ready at all times to absorb a burst.
A defensive floor that keeps baiting from becoming actual defeat.
A fallback plan for a game where nobody ever attacks.

leaders.name: Victoria (Age of Steam)

era_role.ancient_classical: Ordinary civ. No leader advantage whatsoever.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still ordinary. Building the base the bonus will later multiply.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Stacking percentage production across the empire.
era_role.atomic_information: Dominant production for space race or military output.

caveats: Percentage bonuses on a small base produce almost nothing. Empire size before Industrial decides the payoff.
Coal and iron access is a hard prerequisite the ability assumes but does not provide.
Roughly 120 turns with no leader-specific direction at all.
guide_must_account_for: A full generic early and mid game build order, because the kit supplies none.
A strategic resource securing deadline set before the Industrial era arrives.
An explicit statement that the flat early curve is expected, so players do not abandon the plan.

leaders.name: Ba Trieu

era_role.ancient_classical: Constrained development. District placement is the dominant concern.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Defensive fortress with strong terrain-based culture.
era_role.industrial_modern: Still defensively excellent, offensively limited.

caveats: The district restriction is permanent and can make necessary districts genuinely unbuildable in some cities.
Some starts are close to unplayable without waiting on the civic that allows planting Woods.
Every settle decision is also a district decision, made turns before the district exists.
guide_must_account_for: A terrain audit run before every single settle, not just the first.
District planning resolved at settle time rather than build time.
A recovery path for cities that end up unable to host a needed district.

leaders.name: Lady Six Sky

era_role.ancient_classical: Precise tight settling inside the radius.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Efficient compact core outperforming its size.
era_role.industrial_modern: Hard ceiling reached. Efficiency without scale.
era_role.atomic_information: Capped. Wins on quality or not at all.

caveats: The city count ceiling is real and low. Domination is structurally awkward.
Captured cities outside the radius are penalized liabilities, not gains.
The radius is measured from the capital, so a poor capital position is unrecoverable.
guide_must_account_for: A settle map drawn before the first Settler moves, with every city site pre-assigned.
An explicit rule for conquered cities outside the radius: raze, gift, or accept the penalty.
A victory path chosen early, since domination fights the kit.

leaders.name: Nzinga Mbande

era_role.ancient_classical: Claim the home continent quickly.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Consolidated continental empire with stacked yields.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ceiling determined by continent size, which was fixed at map generation.

caveats: A small home continent is a permanent low ceiling with no workaround.
Overseas expansion is actively bad, which removes an entire mid-game option.
You cannot know your ceiling until you have explored the continent's edges.
guide_must_account_for: A continent survey prioritized early, since it determines the size of the whole game.
An explicit prohibition on overseas settling, including tempting captured cities.
A pivot for small continents: a faster victory path instead of a larger empire.

leaders.name: Seondeok

era_role.ancient_classical: Hill-sited Seowons producing reliable science immediately.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Steady, unspectacular science lead.
era_role.industrial_modern: Ceiling shows. Rivals with real adjacency overtake.
era_role.atomic_information: Adequate, not competitive at the top end.

caveats: Isolation forfeits all district adjacency stacking, so the science ceiling is genuinely low.
Hills are a hard requirement for the full bonus and constrain city siting.
Verify the isolated adjacency figure before publishing it; sources cite both +3 and +4.
guide_must_account_for: A hill inventory taken at settle time, since Seowon placement is decided then.
District spacing rules that keep Seowons isolated, which conflicts with normal placement instincts.
A faster victory timeline, because the ceiling does not reward a long game.

leaders.name: Hammurabi

era_role.ancient_classical: Explosive. Eurekas convert to whole technologies.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Eurekas thin out while the halved base science starts hurting.
era_role.industrial_modern: Actively behind. The penalty outlives the benefit.

caveats: The science halving is permanent and never improves. Only the benefit expires.
Later-era Eurekas require conditions that are difficult or slow to satisfy deliberately.
A tech lead that is not converted into something material is worth nothing once rivals catch up.
guide_must_account_for: A Eureka availability audit per era, so the decline is visible before it bites.
A hard conversion deadline: the tech lead must become military, wonders, or territory by a set point.
An explicit late-game plan that assumes a science deficit rather than a lead.

leaders.name: Robert the Bruce

era_role.ancient_classical: Amenity infrastructure build-up before any bonus exists.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Bonuses live, conditional on maintaining Ecstatic.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong while the amenity state holds.

caveats: An amenity crash removes the bonus empire-wide instantly, not gradually.
Luxuries acquired by trade expire, so the amenity state has a renewal schedule you must track.
Wide play makes Ecstatic across all cities practically unachievable.
guide_must_account_for: Amenities as a per-turn monitored stat with a warning threshold, not a build item.
A city count cap derived from available luxuries rather than available land.
A luxury renewal calendar tied to trade deal expiry dates.

leaders.name: Teddy Roosevelt (Bull Moose)

era_role.ancient_classical: Appeal-preserving settlement. Slow, deliberate.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Preserves and appeal yields compounding.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak tourism and passive science.

caveats: No chopping means forfeiting the standard production acceleration lever for the entire game.
Mines and Industrial Zones destroy the appeal the whole strategy depends on.
Appeal-based yields need the Preserve civic to fully pay, which gates the payoff.
guide_must_account_for: Appeal-aware district placement rules that override normal adjacency instincts.
An alternative production plan, since chopping is off the table.
Appeal as a tracked per-tile value that improvements can silently degrade.

leaders.name: Kupe

era_role.ancient_classical: Ocean opening, then coastal settling on high-appeal land.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Pristine terrain yields compounding.
era_role.industrial_modern: National Parks and tourism.

caveats: Starting at sea with no turn-one settle is a genuine tempo loss that must be planned around.
Coastal cities are production-poor, which compounds with the no-chopping restriction.
The appeal payoff arrives late while the costs are all paid early.
guide_must_account_for: An opening ocean route decision with a settle deadline attached.
Explicit acknowledgment of the slow opening so players do not read it as failure.
A production plan that assumes neither chopping nor strong land tiles.

leaders.name: Pericles

era_role.ancient_classical: Envoy accumulation and early culture districts.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Multiplier at full effect across a growing culture base.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong, still contingent on holding suzerainties.

caveats: Suzerainty can be outbid at any time, and the culture loss is immediate and global.
A percentage of nothing is nothing. The multiplier needs real culture districts underneath it.
Envoy competition intensifies as other civs pursue diplomatic victory.
guide_must_account_for: An envoy budget per era, plus a defense reserve for contested city-states.
Culture district construction as a parallel mandatory track, not an optional one.
Suzerainty count as a monitored stat with a response plan when one is lost.

leaders.name: Cleopatra (Ptolemaic)

era_role.ancient_classical: River and floodplain settling with early Food and Culture.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Appeal advantage compounding into culture.
era_role.industrial_modern: National Parks and Seaside Resorts on inverted-appeal terrain.

caveats: Floodplains still flood. The appeal inversion does not prevent the damage.
Dam construction competes for production exactly when growth is most valuable.
River dependency constrains settling more tightly than it first appears.
guide_must_account_for: A flood risk versus appeal tradeoff decision per city, with dam timing attached.
The two-phase nature of the payoff, since early Food and late Parks need different plans.
River availability assessed at settle time across the whole intended empire.

leaders.name: Pedro II

era_role.ancient_classical: Rainforest-adjacent district placement.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Great Person accumulation accelerating.
era_role.industrial_modern: Great Person monopoly across chosen categories.
era_role.atomic_information: Strong in whichever category was monopolized.

caveats: Rainforest suppresses production and is constantly tempting to clear, which breaks the engine.
Great People are contested. A lost race is points spent for nothing.
The refund only applies on recruitment, so patronage spending does not compound the same way.
guide_must_account_for: A Great Person priority list committed to early, since spreading thin loses every race.
Rival Great Person point totals as a monitored value.
A production plan that accepts rainforest penalties rather than clearing them.

leaders.name: Ludwig II

era_role.ancient_classical: Nothing meaningful.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Half-built Wonders as a culture engine.
era_role.industrial_modern: Culture converting to tourism.

caveats: Completing the Wonder ends the bonus. This is the only self-terminating ability on the roster.
A rival completing that Wonder destroys the engine and wastes all invested production.
Production locked in permanently unfinished builds is production doing nothing else.
guide_must_account_for: A designated stall list: which Wonders are deliberately never finished.
Rival wonder progress as a monitored risk, with a finish-it-now trigger.
A rule for when completing is better than stalling, since it changes late in the game.

leaders.name: Kristina

era_role.ancient_classical: No leader advantage. Survive and develop normally.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still nothing active. Great Person groundwork only.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Automatic theming across the empire.

caveats: Roughly 80 turns with no leader-specific direction at all.
Auto-theming needs Great Works, which need Great People, which need early investment with no visible return.
The Queen's Library is a one-time effect, not an engine.
guide_must_account_for: A full survival and development build order for the dormant phase.
Great Person point accumulation started early despite producing nothing immediately.
An explicit note that the flat early curve is intended, so the plan is not abandoned.

leaders.name: Catherine de Medici (Black Queen)

era_role.ancient_classical: Free spy and early diplomatic visibility.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Espionage economy plus combat visibility bonuses.
era_role.industrial_modern: Chateau tourism coming online.

caveats: Spies get caught and killed. The free spy is not a permanent asset.
The visibility combat bonus only matters if you actually go to war.
Chateaux require rivers, so the late payoff depends on early land decisions.
guide_must_account_for: Spy mission priority that shifts by era rather than a fixed assignment.
River tiles reserved for Chateaux from the early game onward.
A decision on whether war is part of the plan, since it changes the value of visibility.

leaders.name: Wilfrid Laurier

era_role.ancient_classical: Tundra survival. Low output, low risk.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Still low output. Building toward the late spike.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. National Parks and tourism spike.

caveats: Surprise War immunity is not immunity to formal war. A prepared aggressor can still declare.
Tundra means low food and production, so everything takes longer than the guide's default pacing.
The late tourism spike needs Parks, which need appeal and Preserves in place well beforehand.
guide_must_account_for: A stated low-output expectation for the first two eras so pacing feels intentional.
A formal war defense plan, since the immunity covers only one war type.
National Park groundwork begun long before the era where it pays.

leaders.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine

era_role.ancient_classical: Great Work accumulation with no visible effect.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Pressure beginning to register on border cities.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Neighboring cities defecting.

caveats: The strategy requires neighbors close enough for loyalty pressure to reach, which is a map condition.
Great Works must be concentrated in border cities, not distributed for safety.
Flipped cities can flip back if the pressure balance shifts.
guide_must_account_for: Border city selection made early and deliberately, since the whole plan concentrates there.
Great Work placement as a strategic decision rather than a storage question.
Loyalty pressure math surfaced to the player, because the mechanism is otherwise invisible.

leaders.name: Peter

era_role.ancient_classical: Tundra Lavras generating early Faith.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Great Writers, Artists, and Musicians accumulating rapidly.
era_role.industrial_modern: Culture and tourism from banked Great People.

caveats: Tundra food scarcity caps city growth, which caps everything downstream.
The pantheon that makes tundra Faith work is contested and can be taken.
Lavra Great Person points still need Faith to convert into actual Great People.
guide_must_account_for: A pantheon race deadline with a fallback pantheon if the preferred one is taken.
A food strategy for tundra cities, since the terrain does not provide one.
Faith allocation split between Great People purchase and religious spread.

leaders.name: Jayavarman VII

era_role.ancient_classical: River Holy Sites providing Food, Housing, and Faith at once.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Population engine compounding.
era_role.industrial_modern: Large high-population empire.

caveats: River dependency constrains settling more than it appears, especially for later cities.
Flooding threatens exactly the tiles the strategy is built on.
Holy Site placement for the river bonus can conflict with optimal adjacency for other districts.
guide_must_account_for: River-first settle planning across the whole intended empire, not just the capital.
Aqueduct and dam sequencing relative to Holy Site placement.
A victory path chosen separately, since population is an input rather than a direction.

leaders.name: Saladin

era_role.ancient_classical: Skip the Faith race entirely. Campuses and expansion.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Religion arrives; Madrasa science comes online.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong combined science and faith.

caveats: The guaranteed prophet is the last one, so belief selection is whatever others left behind.
A late religion means rival religions may already have spread into your cities.
The free tempo only pays if it is actually spent on science and expansion, not banked.
guide_must_account_for: A belief plan that assumes leftovers rather than first choice.
Religious defense against earlier-founded faiths already pressuring your cities.
An explicit use for the skipped early Faith investment, or the advantage disappears.

leaders.name: Gandhi

era_role.ancient_classical: Exploration and first contact. Faith scales with civs met.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Passive Faith accumulating from peaceful relations.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong Faith economy contingent on continued peace.
era_role.atomic_information: Same, increasingly fragile as wars become likelier.

caveats: Output depends on how many rivals founded religions, which you do not control.
Each war zeroes that civ's contribution, so a single conflict has an ongoing economic cost.
Civs you have not met contribute nothing, making early exploration an economic activity.
guide_must_account_for: Exploration prioritized early and treated as income generation, not scouting.
A strictly defensive military doctrine with rules for what counts as provocation.
A contingency for games where few rivals found religions.

leaders.name: Menelik II

era_role.ancient_classical: Hill settling and early Faith generation.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Faith converting into Science and Culture simultaneously.
era_role.industrial_modern: One yield stream funding three victory paths.

caveats: Hills mean low food, which caps the population that drives everything else.
The conversion is a percentage, so a weak Faith base converts into very little.
Rock-Hewn Church placement has terrain requirements that constrain city layout.
guide_must_account_for: Faith base construction prioritized before the conversion is worth anything.
A food supplement plan for hill-heavy cities.
A victory path decision, since the kit funds three without preferring one.

leaders.name: Gitarja

era_role.ancient_classical: Coastal Faith generation from improvements.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Faith-purchased Jong armadas.
era_role.industrial_modern: Naval advantage eroding as ships modernize.

caveats: Continental maps disable the strategy almost completely.
Coastal cities are production-poor, which is why Faith purchasing matters, but it also caps everything else.
The Jong window closes; Faith spent too late buys obsolete ships.
guide_must_account_for: A map viability check before the strategy is recommended at all.
Navy purchase timing set against the obsolescence window, not against Faith availability.
A land plan, since coastal cities alone rarely carry a full game.

leaders.name: Jadwiga

era_role.ancient_classical: Early Encampments stealing border tiles.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Forced conversion and territorial pressure.
era_role.industrial_modern: Less relevant as borders stabilize.

caveats: The ability requires a founded religion first, which gates the whole strategy.
Guaranteed grievances from every affected neighbor, with no diplomatic recovery.
Border Encampments are exposed positions by definition.
guide_must_account_for: Religion founding as a hard prerequisite gate before any Encampment placement.
A defensive plan for exposed forward Encampments.
Acceptance of permanent diplomatic isolation as a stated cost of the plan.

leaders.name: Basil II

era_role.ancient_classical: Religion rush. No military advantage yet.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Cavalry ignoring walls against converted cities.
era_role.industrial_modern: Falls off as cavalry loses primacy.

caveats: Two prerequisites must both be met before the bonus exists: found the religion, then spread it to the target.
Missionaries and Apostles must survive the trip, and they are fragile.
If the target converts away, the bonus disappears mid-campaign.
guide_must_account_for: Religious spread treated as a military logistics step with its own timeline.
Escort planning for religious units moving toward hostile territory.
Target faith status as a per-turn check during the war, not just before it.

leaders.name: Philip II

era_role.ancient_classical: Religion founding. No combat advantage yet.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Peak. Conquistadors against differently-faithed neighbors.
era_role.industrial_modern: Falls off sharply.

caveats: If a target adopts your religion, your combat bonus against them vanishes entirely.
The unit bonus requires a religious unit stacked with the military unit, which is a logistics burden.
The Conquistador window is narrow and era-bound.
guide_must_account_for: A faith check on each target run before declaring, since it determines whether the kit applies.
Paired military and religious units as a standard formation in the build plan.
A caution against spreading your own religion to intended targets.

leaders.name: Tamar

era_role.ancient_classical: Walls and envoy investment. Slow start.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Golden Age chaining at full effect.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong while the chain holds, fragile if broken.

caveats: Missing a single Golden Age breaks the compounding sequence and it does not restart at the same value.
Protectorate Wars require an ally to be attacked, which you do not control.
Wall production is defensive spending that competes with everything else early.
guide_must_account_for: Era score as a monitored per-turn stat with a warning threshold before each era transition.
Ally threat status watched continuously so Protectorate opportunities are not missed.
A fallback plan for eras where no ally is attacked and no Golden Age is reachable.

leaders.name: Mansa Musa

era_role.ancient_classical: Desert settling with weak production and growing Gold.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Purchasing infrastructure faster than rivals can build it.
era_role.industrial_modern: Buying whatever the game requires.
era_role.atomic_information: Strong if the Gold engine held; helpless if it did not.

caveats: The production penalty makes Wonders effectively unavailable for the whole game.
Desert food scarcity limits population, which limits the Gold engine itself.
An economic collapse is unrecoverable, because there is no production fallback.
guide_must_account_for: A Gold income floor defined per era, treated as a survival threshold.
An explicit never-build-always-buy rule, since the instinct to build wastes turns.
Wonders removed from the plan entirely rather than listed as optional.

leaders.name: Yongle

era_role.ancient_classical: Growth infrastructure. No bonus active yet.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Cities crossing the threshold; yields step up sharply.
era_role.industrial_modern: Peak. Percentage yields and per-citizen Gold compounding.

caveats: The payoff is threshold-gated, so progress genuinely looks like nothing until it looks like everything.
Projects consume production that could otherwise be building the housing needed to reach the threshold.
Housing and amenities must be solved before the projects are worth running.
guide_must_account_for: Housing and food infrastructure sequenced before project spam, not alongside it.
Per-city threshold tracking, since cities cross at different times.
An explicit note that the pre-threshold flatline is expected.

leaders.name: Dido

era_role.ancient_classical: Coastal settling and early forward positions.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Loyalty-free expansion onto new continents.
era_role.industrial_modern: Wide multi-continental empire.

caveats: Relocating the capital has real costs and cannot be undone casually.
Coastal cities are production-poor, which the loyalty immunity does not fix.
Forward settling generates grievances from every civ you settle near.
guide_must_account_for: Capital relocation as a scheduled decision point with stated prerequisites, not an improvisation.
A production supplement plan for coastal-heavy empires.
A diplomatic cost budget for forward settling.

leaders.name: Tokugawa

era_role.ancient_classical: Establishing the capital cluster and first internal routes.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Domestic route yields stacking.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong self-contained economy.

caveats: International trade income is forfeited entirely, not reduced. That is a whole mechanic given away.
Domestic routes need many cities to be worth much, so the kit rewards width you must build first.
Isolation reduces diplomatic leverage and information about rival progress.
guide_must_account_for: City count treated as the multiplier on the entire trade strategy.
An explicit prohibition on international routes, since they will look tempting.
An information plan, because isolation means flying blind on rival progress.

leaders.name: Joao III

era_role.ancient_classical: Exploration and first contact with coastal civs.
era_role.medieval_renaissance: Feitorias and high-yield foreign routes.
era_role.industrial_modern: Strong trade economy, still externally dependent.
era_role.atomic_information: Solid if the route network survived.

caveats: Routes require coastal foreign cities that must exist, be reachable, and remain in friendly hands.
A rival conquering your route destinations damages your economy without touching your territory.
Water-poor maps make the extra route capacity nearly useless.
guide_must_account_for: Exploration as a core early loop rather than a preliminary step.
A target city audit maintained over time, since destinations change hands.
Route re-planning triggers when destinations are lost or become hostile.
